chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Do not drink from the milk of the dung-eating camel, and if something from its sweat touches you, then wash it.

key_terms.أَلْبَانِ: milk(s); the plural form emphasizes all types/quantities of such milk
key_terms.الْجَلَّالَةِ: al-jalala: an animal that primarily feeds on human excrement or filth, rendering its products impure according to Islamic law
key_terms.عَرَق: sweat; perspiration — here referring to the bodily secretion of the dung-eating animal
key_terms.فَاغْسِلْهُ: then wash it — a jurisprudential command indicating obligatory washing (ghusl/ghusul as cleaning)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about drinking the milk of a dung-eating camel and its sweat?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through a reliable chain from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), establishes two rulings regarding al-jalala — an animal that primarily subsists on human waste and filth. First, consuming its milk is prohibited (haram), as the animal's diet renders its products impure or at minimum detestable. Second, if the sweat of such an animal contacts one's body or clothing, it must be washed off, indicating its najis (ritually impure) status. This reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential concern for purity and the avoidance of filth in what is consumed or comes into bodily contact.
